Authorization: API keys/OAuth/user consent (depends on service)
Note: Direct integration via documented HTTP/gRPC APIs; high reliability/semantic meaning.
Example: Gmail API: list messages; Calendar API: create event

Authorization: API keys/OAuth/user consent (depends on service)
Note: Actions executed via server-side APIs; not tied to device UI.
Example: Send email via Gmail API; post message via Slack API

Authorization: No special on-device permission; must respect ToS/robots; may require login cookies
Note: UI may change; can break; higher maintenance than official APIs.
Example: Scrape a product page to read price

Authorization: User enables Accessibility Service; must declare canRetrieveWindowContent
Note: Provides labeled UI nodes, bounds, states; may miss custom-drawn/OpenGL content; can retrieve windows with FLAG_RETRIEVE_INTERACTIVE_WINDOWS.
Example: Read current screen buttons and text via AccessibilityService

Authorization: User enables Accessibility Service
Note: Receives UI state-change events (focus/click/text change); good for incremental state tracking and debouncing.
Example: Track when a new chat message appears

Authorization: User consent prompt + foreground service type mediaProjection; Android U+ requires FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MEDIA_PROJECTION
Note: Sees exactly what the user sees (pixels). Secure surfaces may be blacked out; some apps block capture; higher bandwidth/latency.
Example: Capture screen frames for VLM/OCR

Authorization: User grants notification access (settings); service uses BIND_NOTIFICATION_LISTENER_SERVICE
Note: Can observe notification content/metadata; cannot see in-app UI. Useful for background triggers.
Example: Detect incoming OTP notification

Authorization: User grants “Usage access” (PACKAGE_USAGE_STATS special access)
Note: Can infer foreground app switches and coarse activity; retention is limited to a few days for events.
Example: Detect which app is currently in foreground (coarse)

Authorization: Foreground app or default IME; background clipboard access restricted on Android 10+
Note: Good for quick data transfer, but privacy restrictions apply; Android may auto-clear clipboard.
Example: Copy an address then paste into another field

Authorization: Depends on target app exported components / app links; often user gesture required
Note: Most robust when target exposes APIs/deeplinks; limited for arbitrary apps.
Example: Open a map app with geo: URI

Output: Accessibility node actions (performAction: CLICK, SET_TEXT, etc.)
Authorization: User enables Accessibility Service
Note: Acts on specific UI nodes; some apps don’t implement actions correctly; may need gesture fallback.
Example: Click a button by selector; set text into an EditText

Authorization: User enables Accessibility Service
Note: System navigation actions; does not require coordinates.
Example: Go home; open recents

Authorization: User enables Accessibility Service; must declare canPerformGestures
Note: Coordinate-level input; closer to real touch; can be affected by magnification/touch exploration.
Example: Tap at (x,y) when node action fails

Type: Instrumented test runner; adb or test harness
Authorization: Cross-app UI hierarchy extraction for test automation; output is XML; may omit non-standard UI elements.
Note: Dump XML for the current screen

Authorization: Screenshot as Bitmap; mainly for testing; may return null on failure.
Note: Take screenshot during UI test

Authorization: Instrumented test runner; adb or test harness
Note: High-level input primitives; designed for UI testing across apps.
Example: Swipe to scroll list

Authorization: Instrumented test runner; shell-level automation context
Note: Low-level event injection across app boundaries (unlike Instrumentation.sendPointerSync).
Example: Inject raw MotionEvent/KeyEvent in tests

Authorization: Instrumented test runner; uses shell identity (permissions vary by device/build)
Note: Run shell commands similar to “adb shell ...”; useful for glue (am/pm/input/screencap).
Example: Execute “cmd input tap …” from a test

Authorization: Developer options + USB/Wireless debugging; device policy may restrict
Note: Captures display to file/stdout; convenient for remote agent vision.
Example: screencap -p /sdcard/s.png; adb pull

Authorization: Developer options + debugging
Note: Records display to .mp4; default time limit; good for debugging and dataset capture.
Example: screenrecord /sdcard/demo.mp4

Input: adb shell dumpsys / logcat / settings / wm
Authorization: Developer options + debugging
Note: System introspection (activity, window, permissions, etc.); highly device/version dependent.
Example: dumpsys window; dumpsys activity; logcat

Authorization: Developer options + debugging
Note: Shell-driven input simulation using platform input service; best for automation tooling.
Example: cmd input tap 300 400; cmd input text "hello"

Output: adb shell am start / am broadcast / pm
Authorization: Developer options + debugging
Note: Start activities, send broadcasts, install/uninstall; often used to set up flows.
Example: am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW …

Input: SurfaceFlinger/private screenshot or virtual display capture (non-SDK/private APIs)
Type: System/privileged app or ROM integration; not for Play apps
Authorization: Higher FPS / lower latency possible; relies on private APIs and may break across versions.
Note: High-FPS streaming like STF/minicap style

Authorization: Observes raw Linux input events; useful for debugging or building replayers.
Note: getevent -lt

Type: Root; device-specific; often blocked by SELinux/graphics stack changes
Authorization: Legacy/implementation-dependent; modern Android uses SurfaceFlinger/GraphicBuffer; not a stable public interface.
Note: Direct framebuffer grab (legacy devices)

Authorization: Platform signature (signature-level permission) or OEM/ROM control
Note: Inject user events to any window; not available to third-party apps.
Example: System app injecting input for automation

Authorization: Root or privileged context to create /dev/uinput devices
Note: Creates a virtual input device and injects Linux input events; low-level and powerful.
Example: Inject key presses via uinput JSON commands

Authorization: Root; hardware-specific event codes
Note: Directly inject Linux input events; fragile across devices and input drivers.
Example: Replay touch events from recorded getevent logs

Type: Emulator control; host has full access
Authorization: Often easiest environment; can snapshot, run deterministic tests.
Note: Record emulator screen for dataset

Output: Emulator input injection (host or adb cmd input)
Authorization: Emulator control; adb optional
Note: Fast iteration; same APIs as device plus emulator-only controls.
Example: Automate UI flows in emulator
